title: Japan's October CPI: fresh inflation data, not a mortgage reset
summary: Published on 20 November: headline CPI rose 2.3% year on year; both exclusion measures rose 2.2%. These are October price data, not a bank-rate announcement.

takeaways.text: October national CPI rose 2.3% year on year; excluding fresh food, it rose 2.2%.

sections.heading: The new release
sections.text: The Statistics Bureau published October 2026 national CPI on 20 November. Headline inflation was 2.3% year on year; excluding fresh food it was 2.2%, and excluding both fresh food and energy it was also 2.2%. These are different baskets, not three measures of mortgage costs. The release uses 2025=100.

sections.heading: Earlier policy context
sections.text: In his 19 November parliamentary explanation, Governor Ueda described the October decision to maintain the overnight policy target around 1.25%. Further adjustments depend on economic, price and financial conditions, with timing and pace assessed against the outlook and risks. That statement predates today's CPI publication; it is not a response to this release.

sections.heading: Practical interpretation
sections.text: This adds inflation evidence to the policy backdrop but does not establish the next BOJ decision or any lender's mortgage rate. For JPY borrowing, confirm the contract's rate-reset and payment-review dates, or the funding-month terms for a fixed-rate loan. No bank promotion, borrower eligibility or repayment-rule change is verified by these macro sources.

sections.heading: Dates and scope
sections.text: The statistical reference month is October; publication and report writing are 20 November in Japan. The BOJ statement is dated 19 November. Actual source checks are recorded separately in UTC. The CPI links are rolling latest-release URLs and may later display a different month; this report records the October edition read today. No offer-validity period applies.
